sources.measured_here: every bounding box below was measured by parsing the binary STL on disk

units: millimetres (binary STL carries no unit field; slicers assume mm)

frame.axes: +X anterior (snout), +Y the fish’s left flank, +Z dorsal
frame.origin: Single shared origin: the GLB world origin, scaled about it. Object transforms baked into vertices, so loading all 100 part STLs at 0,0,0 reassembles the animal exactly.

scale.standard_length_definition: X extent of every mesh object EXCEPT caudal_fin and caudal_fin_rays (snout at model X=+0.5000, posterior body/skin limit at model X=-0.3528). As specified in the task.
scale.alternative_tail_base_note: If 'tail base' is instead taken as the anterior attachment of the caudal fin (model X=-0.3068), SL would be 0.8068 units and the factor 148.7411 (-5.2%). NOT used.
scale.origin: Single shared origin: the GLB world origin, scaled about it. Object transforms baked into vertices, so loading all 100 part STLs at 0,0,0 reassembles the animal exactly.

hierarchy.organ_from: DERIVED here from the object-name family (dashboard/build-print-view.mjs, ORGANS). The manifest has no organ-parent field; where a part also carries an ontology label it agrees with the family.
hierarchy.level_from: the manifest field level (organ or tissue)
hierarchy.layer_from: the manifest field layer (outer / skeleton / muscle / organ), which also sets the assembly order
hierarchy.no_system_node: One part, swim_bladder, carries the organ_system string "gas bladder (no organ-system node; foregut derivative)". That is the manifest’s own wording and is shown as given; no organ system has been invented for it. No part has a null organ_system in this manifest.

animation.state: one number T in [0,1]: 0 = fully exploded, 1 = assembled. The explode slider is the animation scrubber.
animation.easing: ease-out cubic on each part’s own window [t0,t1]
animation.order: skeleton (vertebrae along the spine, then ribs, skull, girdle, fin rays), muscle, organs, then the outer layer with the skin halves and the fins last

printability.one_line: These 11 parts are single-layer sheets with no interior — zero wall thickness — so a slicer has nothing to fill and they will not print as-is; each needs a solidify/thicken pass (roughly 0.8–1.2 mm) first.
printability.definition: open shell with Euler characteristic 1, i.e. a single-layer disk-topology sheet with no interior. Confirmed for all 11 open objects.
printability.detail: 89 of 100 objects are closed manifold solids and print as-is. The 11 listed are single-layer surfaces: both pectoral fin membranes, all median and pelvic fins, and the skin and skull halves. These need thickening (e.g. 0.8-1.2 mm solidify) before printing - NOT done here, per the task.
not_done: NO joinery, sockets, keys, pins or split for printability
NO boolean union of the overlapping shells
NO support, orientation or bed-fit optimisation
warnings: 89/100 objects are closed manifold solids. The 11 flagged objects are zero-thickness single-layer sheets (chi=1) and will NOT print as-is - they need a solidify/thicken step the hub must add or warn about.
No object has an edge shared by more than 2 faces, so every file loads cleanly; the open shells still slice in Cura/PrusaSlicer/Bambu Studio but render as surfaces, not solids.
The whole-animal file is a non-unioned assembly of 100 shells with interior organ geometry; slicers using even-odd fill rules may show voids where shells overlap. No boolean union was performed.

honesty.hypothetical_note: HYPOTHETICAL: this piece belongs to the design 'winged zebrafish - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion moved toward the flying fish', not to any described animal. It was generated from a parameter set, not observed.
honesty.morphological_not_genetic: MORPHOLOGICAL interpolation, not genetic hybridisation. Averaging two species' body parameters says nothing about whether such an animal could be bred, is viable, or is developmentally reachable; genomes do not average. Flying fish and zebrafish are not crossable. This is a shape, not an organism.
honesty.schematic: Every part’s geometry_basis in the manifest is "schematic" except the pectoral fin membranes and their rays. The shapes are parametric constructions, not scans or segmentations of any specimen.

evidence_backed_proportion.measured_source: median of 49 flying-fish specimens, Daane et al. 2021 Curr Biol Data S1A, recomputed in genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json (quoted from dashboard/public/blueprint3d/data.json, pectoral_fin_L.geometry_basis)
evidence_backed_proportion.delta_reason: a chosen point between the zebrafish placeholder (0.155) and the flying-fish measured median (0.687), near the flying-halfbeak median 0.274-0.388 (Daane groups). Chosen, not measured.

undersize.why: The part set was exported with standard length measured to the posterior skin limit (model X = -0.3528, scale factor 140.7129436712351), which puts SL = 120 mm at the skin tip. The whole-fish file on disk is a later export that measures to the tail's structural base, so it is larger. parts-INFO records the alternative factor 148.7411 for that definition.
undersize.consequence: A kit assembled from the 100 part files is about 4% smaller in every dimension than the one-piece whole-fish print, and the two cannot be mixed. Neither file has been rescaled to match the other.
undersize.not_done: No rescale has been applied here. Scale the part files by the mean ratio above only if you deliberately want them to match the whole-fish print.

honesty.one_piece_note: The glider is a separate object, not a kit part: it is a one-piece hollowed variant of the same body, and nothing in the kit assembles into it. Neither it nor the assembled kit will fly — no flight test has been run on either, and the kit is a solid stack of overlapping shells with no aerodynamic surface, no mass distribution and no trim.

one_piece.title: Whole animal, one piece
one_piece.note: All 100 objects joined into a single mesh. A non-unioned assembly of 100 overlapping shells with the organs still inside, so a slicer using an even-odd fill rule may show voids. This is the file the part set is 4% smaller than.

one_piece.title: Glider variant, one piece
one_piece.note: A hollowed one-piece glider. A separate object from the kit: it is not the sum of any subset of the part files, and the kit does not assemble into it.
